english.html: the witnesses report count for anything: for by what is said above it is sufficiently answered that the witnesses have been validly objected to. Added to which, there are very few tokens given by them which are not found in the said accused, save for the height and the bulk; but as to that, the answer is easy: inasmuch as, as other witnesses not objected to depose, although the accused, when he departed, appeared taller, longer and more slender, nevertheless, since then, by the course of years, he would have filled out in body and grown stronger in the legs.

Frequent experience will keep the reader from being astonished here: for daily we see many men and women slender, thin and delicate in their youth, who nevertheless, by the passage of time and the advancement of age, become stout, fat and cumbersome. And because the examples of this time might be odious to some, I shall have recourse to the most memorable of antiquity. Leo of Byzantium, the sophist, very lean in his first years, became so fat about his middle age that, being ambassador at Athens and mounted upon a high chair to appease some sedition, all the people, seeing him so excessively big and pot-bellied, began to laugh; whereupon Leo began to speak thus: WHAT IS IT that you laugh at, O Athenians, to see me so fat? Know that my wife is fatter still. And yet, when we are agreed, we two can well [lie] in a little bed; but on the contrary, when we are angry, the whole house is not enough for us.
